title: The Quiet Alibi
premise: Bram Eriksen, the coroner of fog-bound Marrow Bay, has spent years quietly proving that three 'accidental' deaths were murders, never telling a soul. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to all three killings, one promising a fourth—Bram realizes the writer knows their secret and is daring them to act. The trail leads to the closed case of Bram's own mother, ruled a suicide twenty years ago, and to the town's beloved founding family, whose inheritance depends on her silence. As the promised fourth death approaches, Bram must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the one person they love: Sheriff Ada Voss, whose father signed off on the original ruling. In the end, Bram catches the confessor—Ada's dying father, confessing through his son's hand—and chooses love over duty by letting the old man die with the truth sealed, while quietly correcting the record on every grave he knows by name.
about_author: Vesper Eastwick is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent a decade reading other people's unfinished stories in probate files. They write mysteries about small towns where everyone remembers everything except what matters.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Bram Eriksen's POV. A quiet morning in the Marrow Bay morgue establishes Bram's gift for reading deaths the police miss, and their careful invisibility after three unofficially solved cases. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence—until two letters arrive in the same envelope, one confessing, one promising more.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Still Bram's POV. The confession letter names three victims only Bram knows were murdered, and promises a fourth within thirty days. Bram begins investigating alone, terrified that exposure will unravel both the cases and their life. The beat shifts from dread to resolve as Bram realizes the writer wants an audience.

chapters.title: What Ada Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Sheriff Ada Voss, who notices Bram pulling files and grows suspicious of the person she's quietly falling for. She reopens a cold file on instinct. The beat is tender tension: two people circling the same secret from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The Halvorsen Inheritance
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The trail leads to the Halvorsen family, whose shipping fortune was settled the year Bram's mother died—a 'suicide' investigated by Ada's father, then-Sheriff Voss. Bram finds her mother's name in the estate papers. The beat is grief cracking open into purpose.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Bram's mother's voice, recovered through her hidden journal. It reveals she discovered the Halvorsens' fraud and planned to testify. The beat is devastating intimacy: Bram finally hears the mother they lost, and understands the fourth letter's promise is personal.

chapters.title: A Confession in Ink
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Handwriting analysis points Ada toward the letters' author while Bram hides their parallel investigation. She confronts Bram about lying, forcing near-confession on both fronts. The beat is heartbreak—the relationship fractures precisely when they need each other most.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following ink and paper trails, Bram discovers the letters are written by young Elias Halvorsen—but dictated by his father, Aldous, who is dying of the same slow poison he used on others. The beat is horror turning to pity: a murderer using his last months to be caught.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The promised fourth death looms; Ada stakes out the Halvorsen estate while Bram races to secure the mother's journal as evidence. Father and son clash over whether the truth should die with Aldous. The beat is rising dread as the deadline arrives.

chapters.title: The Quiet Alibi
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At the Halvorsen house, Bram and Ada converge as Aldous attempts one final murder—his own son, the inconvenient witness—to die with his secrets intact. Bram saves Elias, and Ada arrests her own father's legacy along with the killer. The beat is collision: love and duty forced into the same room.

chapters.title: Correcting the Record
chapters.summary: Resolution, Bram's POV. Aldous dies before trial; Ada must choose whether to expose her father's cover-up and does, at cost. Bram formally reopens their mother's case, carves truth into the public record, and stands with Ada at the cemetery. The beat is peace earned: memory honored, love chosen, every grave finally named honestly.
